question.problem:
Consider the matrix $L$ and the vector $\mathbf b,$ given by 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14240173/assets/a13a7752a224bdabc27558a6a41e2b24d3c7918af1ca4d9cff802dcb54259238.svg)
If $A=LU$ is the LU factorization of some $3\times 3$ matrix $A,$ find the vector $\mathbf{y}$ such that

$$
\{\begin{aligned}Ly=b \\ Ux=y\end{aligned}
$$

is equivalent to $A\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{b}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that since $A=LU,$ we can write

$$
\begin{aligned}Ax=b\,⟹\,{{(LU)}_{⏟}}_{A}x=b.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, setting $U\mathbf{x}=\mathbf{y},$ we obtain

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14240173/assets/605f569e0b4a54d2ca68d7b3330a2a0ebb06dcaba2b7efa911f58dbffd796fb0.svg)

We now solve $L\mathbf{y} = \mathbf{b}.$ Writing this equation in matrix form, we get

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14240173/assets/d259a6740aa32e0e577756375fd85589b815232314511c74dc434a88d0146a3b.svg)

This gives the system of equations

$$
\{\begin{aligned}{y}_{1}=2 \\ {y}_{1}+{y}_{2}=4 \\ {y}_{1}-2{y}_{2}+{y}_{3}=1.\end{aligned}
$$

We can compute the solution to this system using forward substitution, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}_{1} & =2, \\ {y}_{2} & =4-{y}_{1} \\  & =4-(2) \\  & =2, \\ {y}_{3} & =1-{y}_{1}+2{y}_{2} \\  & =1-(2)+2(2) \\  & =3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, 
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14240173/assets/c5198aa83d3976d992b200f63941261f952282fedb241db780c20c12c97e3ba9.svg)
